macros.name: asterisco
macros.doc: \asterisco and its English alias \Asterisk (notice the capitalization) introduce a large centered asterisk.

macros.name: Asterisk
macros.doc: \asterisco and its English alias \Asterisk (notice the capitalization) introduce a large centered asterisk.

macros.name: barretta
macros.doc: \barretta under marks with a short vertical little bar the letter that constitutes its argument; generally it is a djandja but it can be any letter.

macros.name: crocetta
macros.doc: \crocetta with its Latin alias \crucicula introduces a small cross that is frequently found in liturgical Coptic texts.

macros.name: crucicula
macros.doc: \crocetta with its Latin alias \crucicula introduces a small cross that is frequently found in liturgical Coptic texts.

macros.name: djois
macros.doc: \djois(to be written \djois\ as an isolated symbol) is a shorthand abbreviation in liturgical Coptic texts replacing the name \textcoptic{Djois}.

macros.name: dubbio
macros.doc: \dubbio with its English alias \dubious is a macro that receives one or more words as its argument; this string is over braced and a tiny sized question mark is centered on the top of the whole construction.

macros.name: dubious
macros.doc: \dubbio with its English alias \dubious is a macro that receives one or more words as its argument; this string is over braced and a tiny sized question mark is centered on the top of the whole construction.

macros.name: iesus
macros.doc: \iesus (to be written \iesus\ as an isolated symbol) is a shorthand abbreviation in liturgical Coptic texts replacing the name \textcoptic{Iecuc}.

macros.name: sic
macros.doc: \sic is a macro that receives an argument over which the tiny sized word "sic" (without quotes) is superimposed.

macros.name: trepun
macros.doc: \trepun and its alias \threedots introduce a magic sign made up of three dots forming an equilateral triangle; the vertex is at the left and the base lies vertically at the right; if this sign is to be typeset by itself (which I suppose is always the case) it must be written \trepun\ .

macros.name: xc
macros.doc: \xc (to be written \xc\ as an isolated symbol) is a shorthand abbreviation in liturgical Coptic texts replacing the name \textcoptic{Xrictoc}.

macros.name: xcr
macros.doc: \xcr (to be written \xcr\ as an isolated symbol) is a shorthand abbreviation in liturgical Coptic texts.

envs.name: coptic
envs.doc: \end{coptic} is an environment where Coptic text may be introduced that shall be typeset with the Coptic font and hyphenation.
